body:
## Problem

LuaLS struggles with the generics used in Nvim's runtime,
requiring broad diagnostic suppressions. Indexing is also slow.

## Solution

Use EmmyLua for type checks in the build and CI. It offers
more sophisticated type checking, substantially better support for
generics, and much better flow analysis.

Correct the affected annotations. Use `@internal`, supported directly by
EmmyLua, instead of `@nodoc` for shared internal declarations, and
support it in the help parser.

comment_data.body:
Do we want to keep this around (at least for a while) to give people a bit more time to migrate their setup?

(EmmyLua-ls also reads `.luarc.json`, so we can keep serving both audiences by keeping common settings here.)

Of course, it's always nice to clean up, so I'm ambivalent here.
this is not necessary. `K` on the  (`vim.async.Task<R>[]`) already works. If it needs improvements then we can improve it, rather that adding redundant docs everywhere.

comment_regular_data.body: Resurfacing this here (we discussed this before): Last time I checked, EmmyLua-ls had issues with some of the overloads in our API, which lead to downstream warnings. Has that been fixed in the meantime?

> Resurfacing this here (we discussed this before): Last time I checked, EmmyLua-ls had issues with some of the overloads in our API, which lead to downstream warnings. Has that been fixed in the meantime?

Maybe(?). I'd need more specifics. Emmylua had a lot of churn which I worked through. I'm sure it's still not perfect, but I think switching from LuaLS is a net gain at this point. Especially with `vim.async` being added which heavily relies on generics.

> Maybe(?). I'd need more specifics. Emmylua had a lot of churn which I worked through. I'm sure it's still not perfect, but I think switching from LuaLS is a net gain at this point. Especially with `vim.async` being added which heavily relies on generics.

Things like `warning: vim.diagnostic.config() may be nil` (I haven't used emmylua for a while due to these issues and the churn). I'm not mentioning this as a blocker; I just want to add the note here for reference since this is a fresh PR.
`vim.diagnostic.config()` seems to work for me, even without this PR.

I've bundled in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/41750/changes/ad4450bcf42f67f6f697dc31a3be738911920425 to fix all my issues with K help and to remove lots of "See refs". Out of scope for this PR, but oh well.

> `vim.diagnostic.config()` seems to work for me, even without this PR.

It's specifically in stuff like
```lua
function() vim.diagnostic.config { virtual_lines = not vim.diagnostic.config().virtual_lines } end
```
(The warning is for the `vim.diagnostic.config().virtual_lines` call.)

(I'll have to dig up the other diagnostic issues; I tried fixing them at some point but had to give up since our docgen could not emit the ordering EmmyLua expected without breaking the help text.)

**EDIT:** More discussion in https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/34974; https://github.com/neovim/neovim/pull/34974#issuecomment-3088230146 is still an issue.

I currently get: but AFAIK this diagnostic is valid since. ```lua ---@param opts vim.diagnostic.Opts? When omitted or `nil`, retrieve the current --- configuration. Otherwise, a configuration table (see |vim.diagnostic.Opts|). ---@param namespace integer? Update the options for the given namespace. --- When omitted, update the global diagnostic options. ---@return vim.diagnostic.Opts? : Current diagnostic config if {opts} is omitted. function M.config(opts, namespace) ... end ```
